title: The Sigil of Ashvale
premise: Wren Joubert has spent ten years as the invisible ledger-keeper of the Ashvale Guild, recording trades in impossible things while guarding the sealed gate beneath the guildhall. When a century-old book of prophecies names tonight's date as the night the gate opens, she learns the Guild's master, Corvane, has been feeding the entity behind the door—the thing wearing the dead king's crown—to buy his own immortality. Wren must ally with a disgraced prophecy-scribe and the king's exiled heir to unbind the king's soul before the gate devours the city. In the end she seals the gate with her own name written into the ledger, trading her place in memory for Ashvale's survival, and walks away unrecorded but free.
about_author: J. M. Ashgrove is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloging guild records in coastal trading towns before turning to fiction. They write fantasies about ledgers, gates, and the quiet people who keep dangerous things closed.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A night of routine entries in the Guild's impossible ledgers establishes her invisibility and her private ritual of checking the sealed gate. She records a trade that unsettles her: a woman sells her shadow for her son's life. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath practiced numbness.

chapters.title: A Date in Old Ink
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Cataloging a confiscated prophecy-book, Wren finds tonight's date circled in a century-old hand: 'the ledger opens.' She tells no one, but begins pulling records. Emotional beat: the first crack in her belief that invisibility is safety.

chapters.title: The Master's Ledger
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Following the prophecy's references, Wren finds Corvane's private accounts—payments in years of life, all flowing toward the gate. She realizes he's been feeding something. Emotional beat: betrayal curdling into fear as she hears Corvane approaching and hides.

chapters.title: The Scribe Who Read Too Much
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Introduced: a disgraced prophecy-scribe imprisoned in the Guild's depths for reading what she transcribed. Wren, needing her expertise, bargains for freedom with information. Emotional beat: wary alliance between two women who survive by knowing when not to speak.

chapters.title: What Wears the Crown
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin deciphers the prophecy: a king's soul was bound a century ago, and something else has been ruling in his body ever since, sustained by the Guild's trades. Emotional beat: horror at the scale of the deception, and the dawning weight of what Wren has uncovered.

chapters.title: The Heir in the Salt Market
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The prophecy names the king's exiled heir, Emeric, alive and hidden. Wren finds him selling fish under a false name; he wants nothing to do with crowns. Emotional beat: reluctant hope—Wren realizes she can't do this alone and hates it.

chapters.title: An Entry Erased
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Corvane discovers someone has accessed his ledger and begins erasing entries—including, Wren realizes, records of people who may never have existed at all. Her own earliest entries begin to blur. Emotional beat: terror that her identity itself is a ledger line that can be struck.

chapters.title: The Price Already Paid
chapters.summary: Emeric's POV. Emeric reveals his exile was engineered: the thing on the throne had him marked from childhood. He agrees to help only after Wren shows him the ledger entry of his father's binding—and the price his mother paid. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into cold purpose.

chapters.title: Doors That Remember
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The trio searches the guildhall's oldest wing for the original binding ritual. The building itself seems to shift, corridors rearranging to protect Corvane's secret. Tamsin is nearly lost. Emotional beat: the Guild as a living accomplice; loyalty to the institution dies here.

chapters.title: The Guild Turns Its Eye
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Corvane accuses an innocent clerk of the breach and has him 'traded' through the gate as punishment—a public demonstration. Wren must watch and say nothing. Emotional beat: the cost of silence becomes unbearable; her cover story is now complicity.

chapters.title: A Trade Offered in Good Faith
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. Corvane, knowing Wren is the leak, offers her everything: partnership, permanence, her name made indelible. He genuinely believes he's saving the city by feeding the gate slowly. Emotional beat: seductive, reasonable evil—Wren almost understands him, which frightens her most.

chapters.title: The Refusal
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren declines, and Corvane strips her access; the ledgers begin rewriting her history in real time. Tamsin and Emeric extract her through the gate-chamber's service tunnels—past the door, which whispers her name. Emotional beat: exile from the only home she knew, and strange liberation in it.

chapters.title: What the Shadow Remembers
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tracking the shadow-seller from chapter one, they learn the gate's entity keeps what it's fed—the woman's shadow holds memories of the king's binding. Emotional beat: fragile hope; the enemy's own hunger becomes their archive.

chapters.title: The Unmaking of Names
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The entity, through the half-open gate, offers Wren a bargain: it will restore her erased past if she opens the door fully. It shows her the mother she can't remember. Emotional beat: the theme made flesh—survival offered at the price of everyone else's.

chapters.title: Emeric's Choice
chapters.summary: Emeric's POV. Emeric learns that unbinding his father will kill the vessel—the king's body dies either way, and the crown passes to him. He must decide whether he's freeing a father or inheriting a trap. Emotional beat: loyalty vs. truth; he chooses truth, weeping.

chapters.title: The Night of Ledgers
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Corvane, desperate as the prophecy's deadline arrives, begins a mass trade—emptying the debtor cells into the gate to buy one more year. The city's poor vanish street by street. Emotional beat: outrage and urgency; no more time for caution.

chapters.title: Storming the Counting House
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The trio, with freed clerks and the shadow-seller's knowledge, seizes the ledger hall. Tamsin holds the prophecy open; Emeric fights toward the gate-chamber; Wren reaches the master ledger. Emotional beat: chaos, sacrifice, the clerk from chapter ten avenged.

chapters.title: The Gate Opens
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Corvane, dying, tears the gate open himself rather than lose his bargain. The entity—wearing the king's face—steps through. Wren sees the true king's soul, small and caged, behind its eyes. Emotional beat: the climax's threshold; terror and terrible clarity.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: Emeric's POV. The ritual of unbinding: Tamsin reads, the shadow testifies, and Emeric speaks his father's true name. The king's soul is freed and the entity, unmasked, is a crown with nothing left to wear. Emotional beat: grief and triumph braided—the king dies in his son's arms, finally himself.

chapters.title: Corvane's Last Entry
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Corvane, dying, asks Wren to record him honestly—not as a monster, but as a man who was afraid. She writes the true entry, neither mercy nor condemnation. Emotional beat: the theme resolved—truth as the only loyalty that lasts.

chapters.title: The Ledger and the Door
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The gate can only be sealed by a name written into it—someone willing to be forgotten. Wren writes her own name, then tears the page free: an unrecorded name binds without being consumed. She seals the gate and walks out unremembered by the Guild. Emotional beat: the price of survival paid in full, and refused.

chapters.title: Ashvale, Unwritten
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, years later. Emeric rules as a reforming king; Tamsin founds an honest archive. Wren, a nameless traveler, passes through Ashvale and sees her ledgers preserved with a blank line where her name was. She smiles, and keeps walking. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace—freedom outside the record.
